correctness.rationale: For KG(n,2), n>=5, a fixed oriented graph edge e=(A,B) has 6 stabilizer-orbit potential values (t,-t,-u,u,0,0) with t=2(n+1)/[n(n-1)(n-3)] and u=4/[(n-4)(n-3)(n-1)n]. Neighbor counting verifies Laplacian Lh_e=1_A-1_B. Therefore the orthogonal cut projection Q=D^T L^+ D has these gradient columns; cycle P=I-Q. The S_n edge-stabilizer signed symmetries leave only a two-parameter antisymmetric potential and the projection fixing equations force those parameters, hence unique equivariant cut projector. Transpose intertwining gives uniqueness for cycle; averaging any idempotent over signed coordinate isometries proves both globally norm-minimal for every real l_p, 1<=p<=infinity. Absolute gradient orbit counts yield cut 2(n-3)(n+6)/[n(n-1)] and cycle 1+cut-8(n+1)/[n(n-1)(n-3)] at both endpoints. Rational consecutive differences give cut max 5/2 at n8,9 and cycle max 1000/297 at n12. Independently reconstructed integer-scaled Poisson potentials and each endpoint column for every edge of n5..8, checking formulas exactly; this finite check does not prove global all-n minimality.

originality.rationale: Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii arXiv:2305.12582 already develops invariant minimal cycle-space projections, representation uniqueness and examples for Hamming graphs and discrete tori. The general group-averaging principle is not new and should not be counted as originality. Their inspected article does not evaluate KG(n,2) endpoint formulas or maximize them; Johnson graph complements have different edge-coordinate spaces. Closest Resultary Johnson spherical and cactus transportation results also involve different spaces/invariants. Residual risk: a universal strongly regular graph transfer-current/association scheme formula may recover these expressions.
